title: Miami Valley supporting Texas flood victims with supplies, manpower - NewsBreak
text: DAYTON, Ohio ( WDTN ) — Texas is in recovery mode after devastating flooding, and hundreds of organizations across the U.S. are sending help, including from here in the Miami Valley. With search and rescue efforts still underway following flash flooding in Texas’ Hill Country, organizations like the Churches of Christ Disaster Response Team are one of the many teams already on the ground. “I’d say there’s no shortage of volunteer help,” said Matthew Husted, Churches of Christ volunteer. Husted lives outside Huntsville, Texas. He’s one of the people laying the groundwork before more volunteers arrive later this week. “I wanted to be the first boots on the ground in here, to help get them coordinated and help get them set up for the main volunteer force,” said Husted. “What you’re seeing here is a delivery from multiple efforts.” Husted and his team are setting up for the arrival of much needed supplies and more manpower to help clean up people’s homes and get Texans on the road to recovery. “Our motto is ‘First in, last out,'” said Husted. “A lot of organizations can make it in a little quicker than us, however we cover the gap and continue the mission beyond that.” Back here in the Miami Valley, organizations are trying to bring as much relief to flood victims as possible, by gathering supplies and sending essential services to those affected. “They’re providing laundry and shower services. They’re also providing personal cleaning items, baby supplies, water, fans. A lot of the daily essential items people need as they begin this recovery process from flooding,” said Ben Williams, Matthew 25 Ministries chief disaster response officer. Both organizations know its a long road and are asking for as much help as they can, however they can get it. “Together we can make a difference in these people’s lives,” said Williams. “There’s hope at the end of this, that there will be an end to it.” To learn how you can help those impacted by flooding, click here . For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WDTN.com.
